Following 080d82b0.json's confirmed evidence, the work+0x7828 state pointer is never assigned to its own local anywhere in this draft -- every read goes through a STATE macro that re-expands M2C_FIELD(work, void**, 0x7828) textually at each use, avoiding the CSE-induced spill that macro's sibling note documents. The two loop-count guards that gate the whole frame loop compare the scaled member count against a negative bias (`* 20 != -72` on entry, `* 20 + 72` recomputed fresh at the tail) rather than a simplified `!= 0`/`bound` local, matching 080d82b0.c's own preserved-literal-arithmetic precedent for the identical idiom. Residual: matched_prefix=7, and reading the rest of the --align diff line by line found no remaining opcode-class mismatch anywhere -- every `!`-marked row is a register substitution or a stack-slot offset shifted by a constant 4 bytes, and every `+`/`-` pair right after is the same operation reordered or given a different destination register. The root cause is visible at the very top: the reference materializes work into r9 once (`mov r9, r1`) and keeps it there for the rest of the function, while this candidate's build spills it to a stack slot (`str r1, [sp, #52]`) immediately after the ldmia and never recovers it, shifting every later stack offset by 4 bytes and cascading into which high register (r8/r9/sl/fp) holds which loop-invariant value throughout both nested loops. This is the same open, confirmed non-source-shape-controllable register-allocation residual already documented in 080d82b0.json ('why the reference keeps the shared work pointer in r9 while this compiler's candidate keeps choosing a different register for it in places') and 080e7404.json; three targeted experiments this pass (moving the object-field boolean read before vs. after the work+0x7828 write, spelling it as `!!x` instead of `x != 0`, and replacing the if/else palette selection with a ternary) each reproduced or failed to move this residual, confirming it rather than finding a new source-shape lever. Not chased further per the project's guidance against open-ended permutation search on a confirmed compiler-internal residual.

Semantic summary: battle-presentation sub-effect that opens one display window (heap kind 46), copies a 128-word palette/tile block through the generic word-copy trampoline (Func_080072f0 taking the 0x03001388 routine as a trailing callback argument), selects one of two Value_ resource ids for that copy based on whether object's offset-0x18 field is nonzero, then blanks the shared 1024-slot confetti pool at 0x02010000. For each active party member it seeds that member's 128-slot sub-range with particles at the member's rest position plus a random outward kick. The main loop then runs member_count*20+72 times, tracking one member (state offset 8) whose projected motion (Func_080b5098/Func_080b5070) every active particle is later pulled toward; on frame 64 it cues a sound (Func_080b50e8(133)), on frame 40 and again on frame member_count*20+52 it fires Func_080d6888 gate calls, and for each party member whose staggered release frame (member*20) has arrived it cues a portrait/gate call once and then, every later frame, redraws and physically advances that member's still-active particles, retiring each one once it has closed to within +-0xFFF of the tracked member's position on both the x and z axes.

The two structurally distinct Func_080b5098/Func_080b5070/half-value sequences (once per member during setup, once per frame for the single tracked member) are intentionally NOT unified into one helper: the reference computes each independently at its own call site with its own register/stack-slot lifetime, and the setup-phase one reads member_id from the offset-36 s16 array while the frame-loop one reads a single s32 field at offset 8.
